basis: Craniofacial bone-development disorder; hypertelorism does not establish eye damage. Ocular, hearing and CNS abnormalities are occasional.
Mitochondrial metabolic defect; cardiomyopathy 80–99%, developmental delay 4/12, hypotonia 4/12 with abnormal muscle oxidative histology 4/4 support heart, CNS and muscle involvement.
Intellectual disability and language-development impairment define the disorder; dysmorphic features do not establish other organ dysfunction.
Familial thoracic aortic aneurysm and dissection; cardiac and vascular abnormalities share this axis. Stroke is occasional.
Spontaneous dissection directly damages the internal carotid arterial wall; neurologic injury is not established as common in this record.
Hair and nail dystrophy define this ectodermal dysplasia; cleft lip and palate are frequent (30–79%). Conjunctival hyperemia does not establish lasting eye damage.
Localized benign epidermal skin lesion; the definition does not establish systemic nevus-syndrome manifestations.
ALPI-related inflammatory bowel disease directly affects the intestine and is an immune-mediated inflammatory disorder.
Obstruction directly impairs intestinal passage; systemic complications are not defining or consistently common across this umbrella.
BBS1 phenotype includes retinal dystrophy and obesity; polydactyly and developmental/learning impairment commonly exceed 30%. Renal dysfunction is less penetrant in BBS1.
Malignancy of vascular endothelium arising in scalp skin. Lung metastasis is possible but is not established in at least 30% over the typical course.
Neurodevelopmental disorder with persistent impairment; GI dysmotility occurs in 80–99%. Eye movements reflect neurologic dysfunction; adrenal synonyms conflict with the definition.
Retinal tear or break causes detachment of the retina; this is an ocular disorder despite the neurologic ancestor.
Isolated cblD homocysteine-remethylation defect; neurodevelopmental impairment and megaloblastic anemia are common presentations (roughly ≥30%); published numbers are small.
Defined by hearing dysfunction arising in central nervous system auditory pathways, supporting both neurologic and hearing axes.
Chromaffin neuroendocrine tumor arising in sympathetic paraganglia, including adrenal medulla; catecholamine-related hypertension affects most patients, approximately 80%.
Hereditary neural-tumor syndrome; cutaneous neurofibromas and pigmentary lesions characterize NF1, which accounts for most patients. Hearing and ocular injury vary by subtype.
Congenital cardiac/laterality disorder; intestinal malrotation 2/3, asplenia 1/3 and callosal agenesis 1/3 support additional axes. Frequency estimates rely on only three patients.
Peroxisomal lipid-metabolism disorder defined by elevated VLCFAs, retinal dystrophy, cerebral white-matter disease and psychomotor delay.
Alcohol directly injures and inflames gastric mucosa; alcohol exposure does not establish hepatic or other organ disease.
Glutathione-metabolism umbrella; hemolysis, neurologic injury and skeletal disease vary substantially by subtype, without established ≥30% involvement across the group.
Unspecified dominant Ehlers-Danlos syndrome primarily affects joints/connective tissue and skin. Severe vascular injury is subtype-dependent.
Juvenile/adult vanishing-white-matter leukoencephalopathy directly damages cerebral white matter. Ovarian endocrine dysfunction is variable and sex-limited.
Immune-mediated cerebellar degeneration defines the disease. The triggering malignancy is separate; nystagmus and diplopia do not establish direct ocular damage.
Osteonecrosis of the carpal lunate causes collapse and wrist dysfunction; local avascular necrosis does not establish a separate vascular disorder.
